gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much battery energy the parking mode that keeps pre-impact footage uses compared with impact-only standby. VIOFO rates the A329S's impact-only Low Power Impact mode at 0.24 W (5.8 Wh a day), but that mode only starts recording within 2 seconds after an impact. Vortex Radar measured buffered parking recording at 300–600 mA, which is 15–30 times VIOFO's 20 mA rating at 12 V. So a buffered setup has to be sized in hours, not days.
standout_why: I compared against milewitness.com (cited) and productbible.com (rank 1), plus Vortex Radar's own DashCamTalk test thread. Milewitness gives the A329S impact-mode figure ('under 40 mA at 12.6V') and VIOFO's BP100 rating ('up to 32 hours at 3 W'), and its summary confirms it states 'no power draw in watts, Wh per day, parked runtime in hours for the camera itself'. Product Bible rates the modes only as 'Highest / Medium / Low' and gives no watts for any pick. Neither page sets buffered draw against impact-only draw, gives a per-day energy figure, or works out runtime from those figures. I could not open the cited vortexradar.com/best-dashcams page (HTTP 403) or Car and Driver (I ran out of tool calls), so I can't rule out that they cover it.
decides: This confirms ChatGPT's framing and sharpens it. The impact-only low-power modes that stretch parking over days (the A329S's 0.24 W mode, the N4 Pro S 'Power Savings' mode) record after the hit: VIOFO says within 2 seconds, and one N4 Pro S owner reports 7–8 seconds. A driver who taps a bumper and leaves can be gone by then. For hit-and-runs the pick should be a camera running buffered or radar-triggered recording (Thinkware U3000 Pro radar: 7 s before and 13 s after; Vantrue N4 Pro S motion: 10 s before and 30 s after, per Milewitness). The shopper should budget a battery pack or a hardwire cutoff that allows about 13–25 hours of buffered recording per charge, not a week. I couldn't source the parking draw of our linked cameras (Vantrue N5S, N4 Pro S, DDPAI Z90 Pro, N5 Pro, Botslab G980H), so this angle alone doesn't move the pick toward or away from them.

findings.label: Hours of buffered parking recording on a 96 Wh dash cam battery pack (derived)
findings.source_title: Best Dash Cam for Parking Mode: 5 Picks Compared (2026), Mile Witness
findings.note: 96 Wh comes from Milewitness quoting VIOFO's BP100 rating, 'up to 32' h at 3 W: 3 W × 32 h = 96 Wh. Load: 0.3 A × 12.6 V = 3.78 W → 96 / 3.78 = 25.4 h; 0.6 A × 12.6 V = 7.56 W → 96 / 7.56 = 12.7 h. The 12.6 V figure is my assumption (Milewitness's resting voltage for a healthy battery). The 300–600 mA range is from Vortex Radar's thread. For comparison, Milewitness quotes VIOFO's table at 14 h 39 min for a three-channel A329S on the BP100.
